note: Knee OA pain: the rat MIA/MNX models that promised morphine-like analgesia for oral and intra-articular TrkA inhibitors delivered nil-to-modest effects in four Phase 2 trials (2016-2019), none long enough to test the anti-NGF RPOA liability.
label: Osteoarthritis (TrkA)

engagement.note: Pfizer's peripherally restricted pan-Trk inhibitor PF-06273340 was selected on nonclinical pain models; abstract-level, the models are not named in the abstract.
engagement.short: Pan-Trk candidate chosen on rat pain models
engagement.quote: To deliver the safety profile required for chronic, nonlife threatening pain indications, highly kinase-selective Trk inhibitors with minimal brain availability are sought.

engagement.note: PF-06273340 400 mg raised UVB-sensitised thermal pain threshold in healthy volunteers as nonclinical PD predicted; 1 of 5 endpoints, no OA patients.
engagement.short: UVB pain PD translated to volunteers
engagement.quote: The study demonstrated, for the first time, the translation of nonclinical effects into man in an inflammatory pain analgesic pharmacodynamic endpoint using a pan-Trk inhibitor.
engagement.reason: UVB pain translated in volunteers only
engagement.judgement: Call: `same` rests on a healthy-volunteer evoked-pain study of a pan-Trk inhibitor (PF-06273340) that never entered OA trials; high dose met 1 of 5 endpoints, low dose none. In OA patients engagement was never confirmed: Walsh & Neogi 2019 (doi:10.1016/j.joca.2019.07.013) write 'Neither study directly confirmed target engagement in the study participants.' ONO-4474's volunteer NGF-hyperalgesia arm (NCT02454387 Part C) has no posted results and no publication. Registry NCT02260947 has no results posted.

dose.model: Rat MIA and MNX knee OA (oral AR786 30 mg/kg BID)
dose.note: Rat efficacy at 30 mg/kg BID oral; no plasma exposure target or PK was published to carry into patients.
dose.short: Rat dose only, no exposure target
dose.quote: Oral doses (30 mg/kg) of AR786 or vehicle were administered twice daily in either preventive (day -1 to -27) or treatment (day 14-28) protocols.

dose.model: Rat MIA knee OA + monkey NGF-hyperalgesia trough target
dose.note: ONO-4474 100 mg BID was chosen to exceed the rat-MIA/monkey-NGF effective trough; patients fell short of the weak-opioid bar; authors propose 400 mg/day.
dose.short: Model trough met, effect fell short
dose.quote: However, a total daily dose of 200 mg of ONO-4474 did not meet the expected efficacy of a weak opioid, as categorized in Japan.
dose.reason: Rat-derived trough met, effect fell short
dose.judgement: Call: the source states the dose 'was selected to exceed a trough plasma concentration of ONO-4474 that demonstrated a sufficient pharmacologic effect in a preclinical rat OA model and NGF-induced monkey model (unpublished data)', that Phase 1 troughs at 100 mg BID 'exceeded or were comparable to' that target, and then that the effect missed the tramadol benchmark (-5.8 mm, 95% CI -14.3 to 2.8) with a 2x higher dose proposed. I read 'did the exposure target hold' as 'was the model's sufficient exposure sufficient in patients' -> contra. If the rule means only 'was the predicted exposure achieved', this is `same`. Rat/monkey data are unpublished; PK target was set in healthy Japanese men, efficacy read in patients (subjects=mixed). The Japanese Phase 2 has no ClinicalTrials.gov record; Ono's European trial MOTION (NCT02997696) was terminated with no results. Walsh & Neogi 2019 raise the same doubt for ASP7962: 'whether, despite careful preclinical and Phase 1 studies, the investigators advanced the most effective dosing regimen'.

efficacy.model: Rat MIA and MNX knee OA (oral TrkA inhibitor AR786)
efficacy.note: AR786 prevented and reversed weight-bearing asymmetry and allodynia in rat MIA and meniscal-transection OA; a GZ389988 rat-MIA abstract (OARSI 2015) came slightly earlier.
efficacy.short: TrkA inhibitor relieves pain in rat OA
efficacy.quote: Blocking NGF activity by inhibiting TrkA reduced pain behaviour in two rat models of OA.

efficacy.note: Rat MIA promised morphine-like analgesia; oral ASP7962 gave -0.14 vs placebo on WOMAC pain (naproxen -0.67); GZ389988 IA modest, ONO-4474 sub-opioid.
efficacy.short: ASP7962 failed WOMAC pain despite rat MIA
efficacy.quote: Four-week treatment with ASP7962 (100 mg BID) did not improve pain or physical function in individuals with painful knee osteoarthritis.
efficacy.reason: Rat MIA analgesia; ASP7962 failed WOMAC
efficacy.judgement: Call: `contra` rests on ASP7962 (Phase 2a, n=215, NCT02611466; EudraCT 2014-004996-22 results first posted 2018-06-20; abstract-level, full text paywalled). The published rat-MIA data are class proxies (AR786, GZ389988, ONO-4474), not ASP7962, so product_in_model=false and comparison_stated=false for this source. The side-by-side is published elsewhere: Ishiguro 2020 (doi:10.1002/jcph.1470) states ONO-4474 'demonstrated potent analgesic effects, comparable with the effects of morphine' in rat MIA and then 'did not meet the expected efficacy of a weak opioid' in patients (-5.8 mm, CI crossing 0); Walsh & Neogi 2019 editorial (doi:10.1016/j.joca.2019.07.013) compares both trials. GZ389988A (Krupka 2019, doi:10.1016/j.joca.2019.05.028, NCT02845271, no results posted) met its 4-week primary (-7.49 VAS, P<0.05) but not 12 weeks; the editorial attributes part of it to CSF1R affinity and unblinding by injection inflammation, so it does not rescue the model. VM902A (Purdue, NCT02847702) terminated in 2016, unpublished. The failure-after-rat-MIA is a class miss, not an outright reversal, so magnitude is left null.

safety.model: Rat MIA and MNX knee OA (AR786, 28 days)
safety.note: Rat TrkA inhibition reduced synovitis and left osteochondral pathology unchanged; the model is silent on the anti-NGF rapidly-progressive-OA signal.
safety.short: Rat joints unchanged by TrkA block
safety.quote: AR786 treatment reduced MIA-induced synovitis and did not significantly affect osteochondral pathology in either model.

safety.model: Rat MIA and MNX knee OA; rat/monkey toxicology
safety.note: GZ389988 IA: injection-joint inflammation, one tibial stress fracture; ASP7962 tolerated 4 wk; no RPOA seen, but trials ran <=12 wk and excluded RPOA-risk patients.
safety.quote: Greater AE incidence was observed in the GZ389988A group including transient and self-limited injection joint inflammatory reactions with a spike of acetaminophen intake within the first week post-injection.
safety.judgement: Call: `untested`, not `contra`. The class inherited the anti-NGF RPOA story only as precaution: every registry record (NCT02611466, NCT02845271, NCT02997696, NCT02847702) excludes RPOA history/risk, GZ389988 screened by MRI, and exposures were 4 wk oral or one IA dose with 12-24 wk follow-up, so the model's silence on RPOA was never put to a test. Walsh & Neogi 2019: 'Rodent models have not convincingly replicated human RPOA associated with NGF blockade, so it is not possible to exclude this potential toxicity by preclinical testing of TrkA inhibitors' and 'RPOA was not detected in either TrkA inhibitor study reported here'. A `contra` reading (rat IA study silent on local joint inflammation vs injection-site inflammation in two thirds of GZ389988A patients, per the editorial) was rejected because the GZ389988 rat-MIA abstract (OARSI 2015) could not be read to confirm the model reported no local reaction. The ASP7962 rat 4/13-week neurotoxicity study (Kigami 2021, doi:10.1016/j.toxlet.2021.02.018: reversible sympathetic-ganglion neuronal atrophy, no sensory/sympathetic dysfunction) has no published patient counterpart beyond 'ASP7962 was safe and well-tolerated' over 4 weeks (Watt 2019); ONO-4474 patients had hypoesthesia 3.6% vs 1.8% and myalgia 7.3% vs 0% (Ishiguro 2020). No TrkA inhibitor has an FDA/EMA review, so model_filed=false throughout. Two `untested` entries are kept in this cell (not a status change) so the 2019 trial facts are recorded.
